AGENDA
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  JUNE 21, 2022
UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE, MEETINGS WILL BE CONDUCTED PURSUANT TO THE PROVISIONS OF
ASSEMBLY BILL 361, WHICH ALLOWS COUNCIL MEMBERS TO PARTICIPATE FROM A REMOTE
LOCATION WITHOUT LISTING A PHYSICAL LOCATION. TO PROVIDE COMMENTS DURING A MEETING:
YOU MAY ATTEND THE MEETING, SEND AN EMAIL TO: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov, OR JOIN THE
ZOOM MEETING BY CALLING: (669) 900-6833 OR USING THE ZOOM APP WITH THE FOLLOWING LINK:
https://us02web.zoom.us/j/7095732685; MEETING ID: 709 573 2685. THE MEETING MAY BE VIEWED
THROUGH ZOOM, FIOS CHANNEL 32 OR CHARTER CHANNEL 3, OR ON THE CITY'S WEBPAGE AT:
https://www.norwalk.org/city-hall/meeting-agendas-393.
  6:15 PM
  NORWALK CITY HALL/COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  AND VIA VIDEOCONFERENCE

  Rick Ramirez, Mayor
  Ana Valencia, Vice Mayor
  Tony Ayala, Councilmember
  Jennifer Perez, Councilmember
  Margarita L. Rios, Councilmember
  Public Comment: Comments may be made in person, submitted via email at: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov, or through
  the video conference during the designated time on any item on the agenda or on any other matter within the jurisdiction
  subject to the rules of decorum described in Norwalk Municipal Code §2.08.020. The maximum time allowed is three
  minutes.

  Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless
  certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain
  matters for consideration at a future City Council meeting.

  Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the Council:

  • Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
  • Comments should be directed to the City Council as a whole and not directed to individual Councilmembers.

  Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City
  meeting or other services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk's Department, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening
  devices are available at this meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and
  documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability.
  Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring
  that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

  Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after it
  has been posted will also be made available for public inspection.

  Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City Clerk's Department, City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard
  during regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday - Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every other Friday;
  telephone (562) 929-5720. You may also contact the City Clerk via e mail at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

  STUDY SESSION MEETING – 5:00 p.m.
 CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Ramirez

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS FOR CLOSED SESSION MATTERS

CLOSED SESSION

  I.  PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE §54957.6; CONFERENCE WITH LABOR NEGOTIATOR.
  Negotiating on behalf of the City: Jesus M. Gomez, City Manager regarding negotiations with the
  Norwalk City Employees Association.

  II.  PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE §54957.6; CONFERENCE WITH LABOR NEGOTIATOR.
  Negotiating on behalf of the City: Jesus M. Gomez, City Manager regarding negotiations with the
  Norwalk Association of Management Employees.

RECESS

REGULAR MEETING – 6:00 p.m.

CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Ramirez

INVOCATION
  Evangelist Joshua Leyva
  City Reach Church

FLAG SALUTE
  Desiree Romero, 5th Grader
  Dolland Elementary School

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION REPORT

CITY COUNCIL COMMENTS

  a.  Report of City Council Travel

SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS
  United States Army Birthday Cake Cutting Ceremony.

CITY MANAGER COMMENTS

  1.  COVID-19 Update.

  2.  Introduction of New Sheriff’s Captain, Chris Johnson.

  3.  Public Safety Life Saving Presentation.

  4.  Department Highlights - Social Services.

  5.  Bi-Weekly Review.

  6.  Illegal Fireworks Public Service Announcement video.

CONSENT CALENDAR
 Consent calendar items are considered routine matters which may be enacted by one motion and roll call vote.
Any item may be removed from the consent calendar and considered separately by City Council.

  1.  WAIVE READING IN FULL OF ALL ORDINANCES ON THE AGENDA - Staff recommends City Council
  waive reading in full of all ordinances on the agenda and declare that said titles which appear on the
  public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further reading waived.

  2.  MEETING MINUTES – Staff recommends City Council approve the minutes of the meeting of June 7,
  2022. 825-04

  Minutes

  3.  PAYROLL – Staff recommends City Council approve the payroll for the period May 29, 2022 – June 11,
  2022, in the total amount of $1,273,990.27. 630

  Report

  4.  COMMERCIAL DEMANDS – Staff recommends City Council approve the warrant register period May
  24, through June 13, 2022 in the total amount of $5,518,602.26. 640

  Report

  5.  ASSEMBLY BILL 361 FINDINGS - Staff recommends City Council make the following findings:

  a.  City Council has reconsidered the circumstances of the state of emergency.

  b.  Both of the following circumstances exist (i) The state of emergency continues to directly impact
  the ability of the members to meet safely in person and (ii) City Council continues to impose or
  recommend measures to promote social distancing including remote or hybrid meeting
  participation. 825

  Report

  6.  AGREEMENT AMENDMENT NO. 3 - ONLINE APPLICATION TOOLS - Staff recommends City Council
  approve Amendment No. 3 to the agreement with CampaignRep for online application tools not to
  exceed $72,000 annually; and authorize the City Manager to execute this amendment, on behalf of the
  City, in a form approved by the City Attorney. 145-06

  Report

  7.  AGREEMENT AMENDMENT NO. 4 - PRODUCTION OF THE CITY’S MONTHLY NEWSLETTER
  PUBLICATION (NORWALK NOW) - Staff recommends City Council approve Amendment No. 4 with
  Norwalk Printing in the amount of $77,820 annually from July 1, 2022 through June 30, 2023 for the
  printing of the City’s newsletter publication; and authorize the City Manager to execute the amendment
  on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney. 145-03

  Report

  8.  RESOLUTION NO. 22-31 - ADOPTION OF ANNUAL APPROPRIATIONS LIMIT FOR THE FISCAL
  YEAR 2022/23 - Staff recommends City Council adopt Resolution 22-31, A RESOLUTION OF THE
  CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK APPROVING AND ADOPTING THE ANNUAL
  APPROPRIATIONS LIMIT FOR FISCAL YEAR 2022/23. 604

  Report

  9.  RESOLUTION NO. 22-32 – STATEMENT OF INVESTMENT POLICY - Staff recommends City Council
  adopt Resolution No. 22-32, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK,
  ADOPTING THE 2022/23 STATEMENT OF INVESTMENT POLICY AND AUTHORIZING THE CITY
  TREASURER TO INVEST AND REINVEST IDLE MONIES OF THE CITY OF NORWALK IN
  ACCORDANCE WITH THE 2022/23 STATEMENT OF INVESTMENT POLICY. 624

  Report

  10. RESOLUTION NO. 22-33 – ADOPTING PURCHASING POLICY FOR FISCAL YEAR 2022/23 - Staff
   recommends City Council adopt Resolution 22-33, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE
  CITY OF NORWALK ADOPTING THE PURCHASING POLICY FOR FISCAL YEAR 2022/23. 634

  Report

  11. PUBLIC SAFETY COMMISSION APPROVAL OF BLUE CURB AT 14858 FLATBUSH AVENUE - No
  action is required unless the City Council elects to review the decision of the Public Safety Commission
  regarding approval of the blue curb. 265-05

  Report

  12. CORONAVIRUS PANDEMIC – JUNE EMERGENCY OPERATIONS CENTER UPDATE – Receive and
  file. 710-07

  Report

  13. RESOLUTION NO. 22-36 APPROVING AGREEMENTS FOR THE NORWALK SENIOR CENTER
  NUTRITION PROGRAM FOR FISCAL YEAR 2022/23 – Staff recommends City Council:

  a.  adopt Resolution No. 22-36, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK APPROVING AGREEMENTS WITH THE LOS ANGELES COUNTY DEPARTMENT
  OF WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT, AGING AND COMMUNITY SERVICES, AND BETTER 4
  YOU MEALS CATERER FOR THE ELDERLY NUTRITION PROGRAM FISCAL YEAR 2022-/23;
  and

  b.  approve amendment No. 9 with the Los Angeles County Workforce Development, Aging and
  Community Services to fund the Elderly Nutrition Program in the amount of $1,554,100 from July
  1, 2022 through June 30, 2023; and

  c.  approve an agreement with Better 4 You Meals Food Service to provide cooked meals for the
  Elderly Nutrition Program in the amount of $616,242.25 from July 1, 2022 through June 30, 2023;
  and

  d.  authorize the City Manager to enter into the amendment and agreement, provided funds are
  available in the budget, on behalf of the City, in forms approved by the City Attorney. 425-02-03

  Report

APPOINTMENTS

  14. ADVISORY BODIES – Staff recommends City Council make appointments to fill the vacancies on the
  various City advisory bodies. 200

  Report

PUBLIC HEARING

  15. RESOLUTION NO. 22-34 – ESTABLISHING AND ADOPTING THE CITY’S ANNUAL BUDGET FOR
  FISCAL YEAR 2022/23; AND RESOLUTION NO. 22-35 – ADOPTING THE FISCAL YEAR 2022/23
  SALARY SCHEDULE FOR GENERAL AND HOURLY UNIT EMPLOYEES AND EXECUTIVE
  MANAGEMENT AND MID-MANAGEMENT EMPLOYEES – Staff recommends City Council adopt:

  a.  RESOLUTION NO. 22-34, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK ESTABLISHING AND ADOPTING THE ANNUAL BUDGET FOR FISCAL YEAR
  2022/23; and

  b.  RESOLUTION NO. 22-35, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK AMENDING AND ADOPTING FISCAL YEAR 2022/23 SALARY SCHEDULE FOR
  GENERAL AND HOURLY UNIT EMPLOYEES AND EXECUTIVE MANAGEMENT AND MID-
  MANAGEMENT EMPLOYEES. 610
  ORDINANCE

  Report
   16. ORDINANCE NO. 22-1732 AMENDING TITLE 8 (HEALTH AND SAFETY), CHAPTER 8.52 (WATER
  CONSERVATION REQUIREMENTS) OF THE NORWALK MUNICIPAL CODE TO ALIGN WITH THE
  STATE’S EMERGENCY WATER USE REGULATIONS AND PHASE II OF THE NORWALK
  MUNICIPAL WATER SYSTEM’S WATER SHORTAGE CONTINGENCY PLAN – Staff recommends
  City Council introduce by title only, ORDINANCE NO. 22-1732, AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK, AMENDING CHAPTER 8.52 OF TITLE 8, OF THE NORWALK MUNICIPAL CODE TO
  ALIGN WITH THE STATE’S EMERGENCY WATER USE REGULATIONS AND PHASE II OF THE
  NORWALK MUNICIPAL WATER SYSTEM’S WATER SHORTAGE CONTINGENCY PLAN, and
  schedule for second reading. 1070-03

  Report

REPORTS

  17. FRONT STREET FRIDAY NIGHTS EVENTS - Staff recommends City Council receive and file. 415-10

  Report

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

ADJOURNMENT

I hereby certify under penalty of perjury under the laws of the State of California that the foregoing agenda was posted
on the City Hall bulletin board not less than 72 hours prior to the meeting. Dated June 17, 2022.

Theresa Devoy, CMC
City Clerk
